title: The derived adjunction $Lf^*\dashv Rf_*$ on module objects
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring and $f\colon X\to Y$ a morphism of
schemes. The adjunction $f^*\dashv f_*$ on module objects
([def-sfb-module-upper-lower-adjunction]) induces an adjunction

$$
Lf^*\dashv Rf_*
$$

between the total left derived functor of $f^*$, computed on K-flat resolutions in
$\Mod_{\Lambda_Y}$ ([lem-sfb-module-upper-star-kflat-quasi-iso]), and the total right
derived functor of $f_*$, computed on K-injective resolutions in $\Mod_{\Lambda_X}$
([sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]).

proof.text: Work on the small skeletons of the pro-étale sites in the size convention of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. For either scheme $T=X,Y$, put $\mathcal C_T=\Sh(T_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)$. Its closed symmetric monoidal structure and the preservation of colimits by either tensor functor are [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]. Its Grothendieck abelian structure follows from [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck] applied to the constant sheaf of rings $\mathbf Z$: a sheaf of abelian groups has exactly one compatible $\mathbf Z$-module structure, namely repeated addition. Thus this is the same category, with the same morphisms.

source.place: Part 4: abelian sheaves on the pro-étale site

proof.text: For an object $U$ of the chosen site let $\mathbf Z_U$ be the sheafified free abelian presheaf on $U$. Its tensor functor preserves finite limits by [lem-weil-pbc-free-sheaf-flat], taking $P=\mathbf Z$; tensoring with $\mathbf Z$ is the identity. It also preserves cokernels by [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor], so is exact; symmetry gives exactness on the other side. Thus $\mathbf Z_U$ is flat. Define $P_T(M)=\bigoplus_{(U,s),\ s\in M(U)}\mathbf Z_U$, with evaluation $P_T(M)\to M$. A morphism $h:M\to N$ sends the summand $(U,s)$ identically to the summand $(U,h_U(s))$, so this is a functor and evaluation is natural. Evaluation is an epimorphism: each section $s\in M(U)$ is the image of the generator indexed by $(U,s)$. Tensor distributes over this coproduct by the closedness in [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]. Direct sums of exact sequences are exact here: write a direct sum as the filtered colimit of its finite subsums, using exact filtered colimits from [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck]. Hence every $P_T(M)$ is flat. This supplies the functorial flat resolutions required below.

source.place: Part 4: the functorial epimorphism from the sum of free abelian sheaves

proof.text: By [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], $\Lambda_T=p_T^*\Lambda$ is a commutative ring object because $\Lambda$ is commutative. By [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], $\Mod_{\Lambda_T}$ is the category of module objects over the pulled-back commutative ring object in $\mathcal C_T$. Apply [lem-sfb-modobj-grothendieck] to get its Grothendieck abelian structure, [def-sfb-modobj-symmetric-tensor] for the symmetric relative tensor product, and [def-sfb-modobj-internal-hom] for its closedness. Their hypotheses hold by step 1: $\mathcal C_T$ is closed symmetric monoidal and Grothendieck abelian, and tensor preserves colimits in each variable, hence finite biproducts and is additive. Apply [lem-sfb-modobj-flat-resolutions] to the functor of step 2 to obtain functorial flat resolutions in $\Mod_{\Lambda_T}$. The closed relative tensor product preserves colimits in each variable by [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits]. It preserves zero objects and finite biproducts and therefore is additive: addition of two maps is the composite of their direct sum with the diagonal and codiagonal, all of which are preserved. This Grothendieck category has countable coproducts and exact filtered colimits. The poset $(\mathbf Z,\leq)$ is filtered (any two integers have their maximum as an upper bound), so its indexed colimits are exact. Thus all the tensor-additivity, countable-coproduct and exact $\mathbf Z$-indexed-colimit hypotheses in [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories] hold.

source.place: Parts 3 and 4: module Grothendieck, closed monoidal, and flat-resolution structures

proof.text: Take $F=f^*:\Mod_{\Lambda_Y}\to\Mod_{\Lambda_X}$ and $G=f_*:\Mod_{\Lambda_X}\to\Mod_{\Lambda_Y}$. They are additive by [def-sfb-module-upper-star] and [def-sfb-module-lower-star], and [def-sfb-module-upper-lower-adjunction] supplies $F\dashv G$. These are the full underived module functors, including extension and restriction of scalars, rather than the underlying abelian-sheaf functors.

source.place: Proof: specialization of the general derived adjunction

proof.text: The termwise functor $F$ sends quasi-isomorphisms between K-flat complexes to quasi-isomorphisms by [lem-sfb-module-upper-star-kflat-quasi-iso]. The left-derived-functor clause of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories], with the structural hypotheses checked in step 3, therefore constructs $LF$ on the unbounded derived categories, computed on K-flat resolutions in $\Mod_{\Lambda_Y}$. The right-derived-functor clause of the same node applies to $G$: the Grothendieck category $\Mod_{\Lambda_X}$ from step 3 has K-injective resolutions. It constructs $RG$ on the unbounded derived categories, computed on K-injective resolutions in $\Mod_{\Lambda_X}$.

source.place: Proof: specialization of the general derived adjunction

proof.text: Apply the Derived adjunctions clause of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories] to $F\dashv G$ from step 4. The source of $F$ has all the monoidal and flat-resolution hypotheses by step 3, its K-flat quasi-isomorphism hypothesis is step 5, and its target has K-injective resolutions by step 5. This gives the induced adjunction $LF\dashv RG$, hence $Lf^*\dashv Rf_*$. Define the adjunction in this node to be this specialization of the general construction. Its left and right functors are exactly the total derived functors of the composites in step 4, with the resolutions specified in step 5; no factorization through derived abelian sheaves is used.

source.place: Proof: specialization of the general derived adjunction

proof_origin.place: Proof; with the module-category hypotheses expanded from the proof of sk-prop-sfb-module-category, Parts 3–4
